stemMd: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The evidence for a single campaign of cutting rests mainly on the beams that kept their outermost ring.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The two beams with joints that fit nothing in the present frame are older than the rest of the roof.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The five squared beams were felled before 1446, some years earlier than the other fourteen dated beams.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The abbey's records of a gradual replacement over a century were shown by the ring dates to be false.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The nineteen dated beams prove that the roof was built in 1448, the latest of the recorded felling years.

explanationMd:
An **inference** question: the right choice is not stated, but the passage's own reasoning forces it.

**What to notice first.** Only the fourteen beams that "had kept their outermost ring" have exact felling years (1446 to 1448). The second paragraph has already explained that for a squared beam the last surviving ring gives only a year "before which the tree cannot have been felled".

**The step that settles it.** The claim that most timber was cut in a single campaign needs felling dates that sit close together. The fourteen supply them. The five squared beams supply only lower limits, which are compatible with the campaign but cannot show it. So the evidence for the campaign rests mainly on the fourteen beams with an intact outer ring.

**Testing the others.** The tempting mistake is to read the squared beams' dates (1431 to 1444) as felling dates; the passage has told you they are not. The remaining three choices each overstate: the marked beams are not said to be older, the records are not said to be false, and the roof is explicitly left undated.

**How to check.** For each choice ask "which sentence of the passage forces this?" Only one choice has an answer to that question.

distractorRationale.c: Their last surviving rings date from 1431 to 1444, but squaring removed the outer rings, so those dates only give years before which the trees cannot have been felled. The trees may have been felled later, possibly in the same years as the other fourteen, so nothing shows they are earlier.
distractorRationale.b: The passage says only that "whatever their dates" the marked beams cannot show when the frame was made. The joints hint that the beams may have been reused, but nothing is said about how old they are.
distractorRationale.d: The passage says the records "had implied" gradual replacement over a century and that the dates "suggested" something different. That is a suggestion, not a demonstration, and the researchers declined to date the roof.
distractorRationale.e: The researchers "declined to announce a date for the roof", and the passage explains why: reused beams would still give their original felling dates. 1448 is only the latest felling year among the fourteen beams with an outer ring; the choice claims a certainty the passage denies.

accessibilityText: A question about the accompanying scientific passage on dating timber by its growth rings and the roof of the abbey of San Lorenzo in Valdera. It asks which of five statements can be inferred from the passage. The five choices say: that the evidence for a single campaign of cutting rests mainly on the beams that kept their outermost ring; that the two beams with joints that fit nothing in the present frame are older than the rest of the roof; that the five squared beams were felled before 1446, some years earlier than the other fourteen dated beams; that the abbey's records of a gradual replacement over a century were shown by the ring dates to be false; and that the nineteen dated beams prove that the roof was built in 1448, the latest of the recorded felling years.

provenance.notes: Original item written against the original passage polito-til-a-passage-roof-rings-301, authored alongside it. Every distractor rests on a named misreading of that passage.

review.author: polito-til-a-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Only the 14 beams with an outermost ring give actual felling years, all clustered in 1446-48; the squared beams give only earliest-possible dates. So the single-campaign pattern rests mainly on those 14. C inverts the terminus post quem, B and E are contradicted ('whatever their dates', 'declined to announce'), and D overstates 'suggested'. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-bocconi-verbal-logic-tila-reading-run1) reached the same answer: Only the 14 beams that kept their outermost ring give actual felling years (1446-48). The 5 squared beams give only earliest-possible years plus a sapwood range, so the tight clustering that suggests a single campaign comes mainly from the 14. B: the marked beams may be reused, but they are not said to be older ('whatever their dates'). C reverses the meaning of the last surviving ring, which gives a not-before year. D: the dates only 'suggested' the records were wrong. E: the researchers declined to give a date.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: only the fourteen beams with an intact outer ring have exact felling years, and the squared beams give lower limits only, so the single-campaign evidence rests mainly on the fourteen; the squared beams' last-ring dates cannot be read as felling dates, and the other choices claim more than the passage states.
